title: Pulse wave-driven machine learning for the non-invasive assessment of coronary artery calcification in patients with end-stage renal disease undergoing hemodialysis.
summary: Pulse-wave features and machine-learning models assessed CT-defined coronary artery calcification severity in 58 hemodialysis patients; this is an exploratory non-invasive adjunct result. The result is reported in BioMedical Engineering OnLine. The study does not establish generalization beyond its reported setting or prospective real-world benefit.
ai_technology: A gradient-boosting decision tree classified coronary artery calcification severity from radial-artery pulse-wave features in hemodialysis patients.

evidence.tested: Pulse-wave features and machine-learning models assessed CT-defined coronary artery calcification severity in 58 hemodialysis patients; this is an exploratory non-invasive adjunct result.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and prospective real-world benefit are not established in the reviewed study.
